# Scope

This companion exposes the complete executable code behind the final report.
All imports begin with unchanged instructor CSV files. This annotated analysis
companion generates the tables and figures; the final Methods, Results and
References narrative must also be submitted as required by the course.

```{r prepare-data}
# All cleaning starts from the three unchanged instructor CSV files.
# Check dependencies before loading packages; install missing packages separately.
required_packages <- c("ggplot2", "dplyr", "tidyr", "patchwork", "rlang",
                       "knitr", "rmarkdown")
missing_packages <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace,
                                            logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop("Install these packages before knitting: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
dir.create("results", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("figures", showWarnings = FALSE)

cov_path <- "E:/桌面/raw/GSE85307_covar-1.csv"
if (!file.exists(cov_path)) cov_path <- "data/raw/GSE85307_covar.csv"
expr_path <- "E:/桌面/raw/GSE85307_geneExpression.csv"
gene_path <- "E:/桌面/raw/GSE85307_geneNames.csv"
# Stop early and identify missing files rather than failing midway through import.
input_paths <- c(cov_path, expr_path, gene_path)
missing_files <- input_paths[!file.exists(input_paths)]
if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop("Missing input files: ", paste(missing_files, collapse = ", "),
       ". Keep this Rmd in the project root with data/raw underneath it.")
}
covar_raw <- read.csv(cov_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
expr_raw <- read.csv(expr_path,
                     row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE)
link_raw <- read.csv(gene_path,
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

# Remove the label before the FIRST colon, then trim surrounding whitespace.
strip_label <- function(x) trimws(sub("^[^:]*:\\s*", "", x, perl = TRUE))
clean <- covar_raw
for (v in setdiff(names(clean), c("subjectID", "geoID"))) {
  clean[[v]] <- strip_label(clean[[v]])
}
num_vars <- c("mat_age_yrs", "delivery_gestAge_wks",
              "sampleCollection_gestAge_wks", "mat_BMI", "mat_vitD")
for (v in num_vars) {
  before <- clean[[v]]
  clean[[v]] <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(before))
  if (any(is.na(clean[[v]]) & !is.na(before))) stop("Numeric conversion failed: ", v)
}
# Sample identifiers must be present, nonblank and unique before matching.
stopifnot(!anyNA(clean$geoID), !anyNA(clean$subjectID),
          all(nzchar(trimws(clean$geoID))), all(nzchar(trimws(clean$subjectID))))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(clean$geoID), !anyDuplicated(clean$subjectID),
          !anyDuplicated(colnames(expr_raw)), !anyDuplicated(rownames(expr_raw)),
          !anyDuplicated(link_raw$PROBEID), !anyDuplicated(link_raw$GENE),
          setequal(clean$geoID, colnames(expr_raw)),
          all(clean$preg_preeclampsia %in% c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
          all(clean$mat_asthma %in% c("0", "1")))
expr <- as.matrix(expr_raw)
stopifnot(is.numeric(expr), all(is.finite(expr)))

# Match expression columns by ID: never assume the input order is the same.
expr <- expr[, match(clean$geoID, colnames(expr)), drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(colnames(expr), clean$geoID))
map <- link_raw[match(rownames(expr), as.character(link_raw$PROBEID)), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(map$GENE), identical(as.character(map$PROBEID), rownames(expr)))
rownames(expr) <- map$GENE

# Study-specific threshold from Mirzakhani et al. (2016), NOT a diagnostic rule.
clean <- clean %>% mutate(
  preg_preeclampsia = factor(preg_preeclampsia, levels = c("Normal", "Preeclampsia")),
  vitD_group = factor(ifelse(mat_vitD < 30, "<30 ng/mL", ">=30 ng/mL"),
                      levels = c("<30 ng/mL", ">=30 ng/mL")),
  mat_asthma = factor(mat_asthma, levels = c("0", "1"), labels = c("No", "Yes")),
  batch_Microarray = factor(batch_Microarray))
# Preserve all 157 samples; do not remove outliers just to improve the plot.
all_genes <- as.data.frame(t(expr), check.names = FALSE)
analysis_data <- bind_cols(clean, all_genes)
selected_genes <- c("CYP24A1", "PTX3", "CXCR2")
heat_genes <- c(selected_genes, "JAK2", "LYN", "SOCS5", "IL7", "IL2", "TGM2", "TIMP1")
stopifnot(all(heat_genes %in% rownames(expr)), nrow(analysis_data) == 157L)
missing_table <- data.frame(variable = names(clean), missing = colSums(is.na(clean)))
# This analysis retains all samples and does not silently impute missing values.
stopifnot(sum(missing_table$missing) == 0,
          all(vapply(clean[num_vars], function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1))))
write.csv(missing_table, "results/missingness.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(map, "results/probe_gene_mapping_used.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(clean, "results/clean_covariates.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(as.data.frame(table(clean$preg_preeclampsia, clean$vitD_group)),
          "results/group_counts.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(data.frame(file = input_paths,
                     md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_paths))),
          "results/input_checksums.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

# Reusable plotting function

```{r function}
# Return a named list of three ggplot objects for each requested gene.
plot_gene_panels <- function(data, genes, continuous, categorical) {
  genes <- unlist(genes, use.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.character(continuous) || anyNA(continuous) ||
      !is.character(categorical) || anyNA(categorical) ||
      anyNA(genes) || anyDuplicated(categorical)) {
    stop("Use nonmissing column names and two distinct categorical variables.")
  }
  if (!is.data.frame(data) || !is.character(genes) || length(genes) < 1L ||
      length(continuous) != 1L || length(categorical) != 2L) {
    stop("Supply a data frame, >=1 gene, one continuous name, and two categorical names.")
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(genes)) stop("Gene names must be unique.")
  if (!all(c(genes, continuous, categorical) %in% names(data))) stop("Unknown column name.")
  if (!is.numeric(data[[continuous]]) || !all(vapply(data[genes], is.numeric, logical(1)))) {
    stop("Gene expression and the continuous covariate must be numeric.")
  }
  if (!all(vapply(data[categorical], function(x) is.factor(x) || is.character(x), logical(1)))) {
    stop("Categorical covariates must be factors or character columns.")
  }
  out <- list()
  for (gene in genes) {
    # Filter only the columns needed for this gene and state the plotted n.
    d <- data[complete.cases(data[, c(gene, continuous, categorical)]), , drop = FALSE]
    numeric_cols <- c(gene, continuous)
    if (!all(vapply(d[numeric_cols], function(x) all(is.finite(x)), logical(1)))) {
      stop("Nonfinite values in expression or continuous covariate for ", gene)
    }
    if (length(unique(d[[continuous]])) < 2L) {
      stop("The continuous covariate must have at least two distinct values.")
    }
    if (nrow(d) < 3L) stop("Too few complete observations for ", gene)
    xlab <- if (continuous == "mat_vitD") "Baseline 25(OH)D (ng/mL)" else continuous
    ylab <- paste0(gene, " expression (provided scale)")
    n_txt <- paste("n =", nrow(d))
    style <- theme_classic(base_size = 11, base_family = "sans") +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
            plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey35"),
            legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank(),
            strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey94", colour = NA),
            strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
            plot.margin = margin(10, 14, 10, 10))
    hist <- ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[gene]])) +
      geom_histogram(bins = 24, fill = "#337C8E", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.25) +
      labs(title = paste(gene, "expression distribution"), subtitle = n_txt,
           x = ylab, y = "Number of participants") + style
    scatter <- ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[continuous]], y = .data[[gene]])) +
      geom_point(colour = "#337C8E", alpha = 0.65, size = 1.7) +
      geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE,
                  colour = "#B65E27", fill = "#E4B48B", linewidth = 0.8) +
      labs(title = paste(gene, "and", if (continuous == "mat_vitD") "baseline vitamin D" else continuous), subtitle = n_txt,
           x = xlab, y = ylab) + style
    # Use both categories: x = outcome; facet and colour = vitamin D group.
    counts <- d %>% group_by(across(all_of(categorical))) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")
    ymax <- max(d[[gene]])
    span <- diff(range(d[[gene]])); if (span == 0) span <- 1
    counts$label_y <- ymax + 0.08 * span
    box <- ggplot(d, aes(x = .data[[categorical[1]]], y = .data[[gene]],
                         fill = .data[[categorical[2]]])) +
      geom_boxplot(width = 0.55, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.65, linewidth = 0.45) +
      geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 103),
                 shape = 21, size = 1.3, alpha = 0.6, stroke = 0.2) +
      geom_text(data = counts, aes(x = .data[[categorical[1]]], y = label_y,
                                  label = paste0("n = ", n)),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1) +
      facet_wrap(vars(!!rlang::sym(categorical[2]))) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = rep(c("#337C8E", "#D5A13B", "#7D5596", "#AD4E32", "#57A773", "#C27D9F"),
        length.out = length(unique(d[[categorical[2]]])))) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.07, 0.17))) +
      labs(title = paste(gene, "by", paste(categorical, collapse = " and ")), subtitle = n_txt,
           x = if (categorical[1] == "preg_preeclampsia") "Pregnancy outcome" else categorical[1], y = ylab) + style + theme(legend.position = "none")
    out[[gene]] <- list(histogram = hist, scatterplot = scatter, boxplot = box)
  }
  out
}

# Save vector PDF and 300-dpi PNG versions for manuscripts and presentations.
save_gene_panels <- function(panels) {
  for (gene in names(panels)) for (kind in names(panels[[gene]])) {
    base <- file.path("figures", paste(gene, kind, sep = "_"))
    w <- if (kind == "boxplot") 8.2 else 7
    ggsave(paste0(base, ".pdf"), panels[[gene]][[kind]], width = w, height = 4.7)
    ggsave(paste0(base, ".png"), panels[[gene]][[kind]], width = w, height = 4.7, dpi = 300)
  }
}
```

```{r gene-plots}
panels <- plot_gene_panels(analysis_data, selected_genes, "mat_vitD",
                          c("preg_preeclampsia", "vitD_group"))
save_gene_panels(panels)
```

# Summary table, heatmap, ECDF and software citations

```{r final-outputs}
# Table 1: three continuous covariates, stratified by pregnancy outcome.
cont <- c("mat_vitD", "mat_age_yrs", "mat_BMI")
labels <- c("25(OH)D (ng/mL)", "Age (years)", "BMI (kg/m2)")
summary_table <- data.frame(Characteristic = c(
  as.vector(rbind(paste0(labels, ": mean (SD)"), paste0(labels, ": median [Q1, Q3]"))),
  "25(OH)D <30 ng/mL, n (%)", "25(OH)D >=30 ng/mL, n (%)"), check.names = FALSE)
for (grp in c("Overall", levels(clean$preg_preeclampsia))) {
  d <- if (grp == "Overall") clean else filter(clean, preg_preeclampsia == grp)
  vals <- character()
  for (v in cont) {
    z <- d[[v]]; q <- quantile(z, c(.25, .5, .75))
    vals <- c(vals, sprintf("%.2f (%.2f)", mean(z), sd(z)),
              sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]", q[2], q[1], q[3]))
  }
  counts <- table(d$vitD_group)
  vals <- c(vals, sprintf("%d (%.1f)", counts, 100 * counts / nrow(d)))
  summary_table[[paste0(grp, " (n=", nrow(d), ")")]] <- vals
}
write.csv(summary_table, "results/Table1.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Descriptive summaries: genes are not chosen by p-value.
gene_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(selected_genes, function(g) {
  y <- analysis_data[[g]]
  fit <- lm(y ~ mat_vitD, data = analysis_data)
  ci <- confint(fit)[2, ]
  data.frame(gene = g, n = length(y), mean = mean(y), sd = sd(y),
             median = median(y), Q1 = quantile(y, .25), Q3 = quantile(y, .75),
             min = min(y), max = max(y),
             pearson_r_descriptive = cor(analysis_data$mat_vitD, y),
             slope_per_10ng = 10 * coef(fit)[2], CI_low = 10 * ci[1], CI_high = 10 * ci[2])
}))
write.csv(gene_summary, "results/gene_summaries.csv", row.names = FALSE)
group_gene_summary <- analysis_data %>% group_by(preg_preeclampsia, vitD_group) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), across(all_of(selected_genes),
    list(median = median, Q1 = ~quantile(.x, .25), Q3 = ~quantile(.x, .75))), .groups = "drop")
write.csv(group_gene_summary, "results/gene_group_summaries.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Ten fixed available genes; row-wise z-scores; Euclidean/complete clustering.
m <- expr[heat_genes, , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(all(apply(m, 1, sd) > 0))
z <- t(scale(t(m)))
row_hc <- hclust(dist(z), method = "complete")
col_hc <- hclust(dist(t(z)), method = "complete")
gene_order <- rownames(z)[row_hc$order]
sample_order <- colnames(z)[col_hc$order]
heat_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(z), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(heat_df) <- c("gene", "geoID", "z")
heat_df$x <- match(heat_df$geoID, sample_order)
heat_df$gene <- factor(heat_df$gene, levels = rev(gene_order))
# Convert sample clustering to dendrogram segments aligned with heatmap columns.
segments <- data.frame(x = numeric(), xend = numeric(), y = numeric(), yend = numeric())
leaf_positions <- match(seq_along(col_hc$order), col_hc$order)
walk <- function(node) {
  if (node < 0) return(c(leaf_positions[-node], 0))
  a <- walk(col_hc$merge[node, 1]); b <- walk(col_hc$merge[node, 2])
  h <- col_hc$height[node]
  segments <<- rbind(segments,
    data.frame(x = c(a[1], b[1], a[1]), xend = c(a[1], b[1], b[1]),
               y = c(a[2], b[2], h), yend = c(h, h, h)))
  c(mean(c(a[1], b[1])), h)
}
invisible(walk(nrow(col_hc$merge)))
xscale <- scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, ncol(z) + 0.5), expand = c(0, 0))
dend <- ggplot(segments) + geom_segment(aes(x=x, xend=xend, y=y, yend=yend),
  linewidth = .25, colour = "grey30") + xscale + theme_void()
ann <- clean[match(sample_order, clean$geoID), c("geoID", "preg_preeclampsia", "vitD_group")]
stopifnot(identical(ann$geoID, sample_order))
ann$x <- seq_len(nrow(ann))
ann_long <- pivot_longer(ann, cols = c(preg_preeclampsia, vitD_group),
                         names_to = "track", values_to = "value")
ann_long$track <- factor(ann_long$track, levels = c("vitD_group", "preg_preeclampsia"),
                         labels = c("Vitamin D", "Outcome"))
tracks <- ggplot(ann_long, aes(x, track, fill = value)) + geom_tile() + xscale +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Normal"="#4393A7", "Preeclampsia"="#B55F38",
                               "<30 ng/mL"="#595959", ">=30 ng/mL"="#D5A13B")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Sample annotations") + theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right", plot.margin = margin(0, 5, 0, 5))
heat <- ggplot(heat_df, aes(x, gene, fill = z)) + geom_tile() + xscale +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#2166AC", mid = "#FAFAFA", high = "#B2182B",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "Gene-wise\nz-score") +
  labs(x = "Participants in hierarchical cluster order", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), legend.position = "right")
heatmap_plot <- (dend / tracks / heat) + plot_layout(heights = c(1.2, .65, 4)) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Ten-gene expression profile in early pregnancy",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14)))
ggsave("figures/heatmap.pdf", heatmap_plot, width = 10, height = 6.4)
ggsave("figures/heatmap.png", heatmap_plot, width = 10, height = 6.4, dpi = 300)
write.csv(data.frame(cluster_position = seq_along(sample_order), geoID = sample_order),
          "results/heatmap_sample_order.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Additional candidate: empirical cumulative distribution function (ECDF).
ecdf_data <- analysis_data %>% select(geoID, preg_preeclampsia, vitD_group, all_of(selected_genes)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(selected_genes), names_to = "gene", values_to = "expression") %>%
  mutate(group = interaction(preg_preeclampsia, vitD_group, sep = " | "))
ecdf_n <- ecdf_data %>% distinct(geoID, group) %>% count(group)
legend_labels <- setNames(paste0(ecdf_n$group, " (n=", ecdf_n$n, ")"), ecdf_n$group)
ecdf_plot <- ggplot(ecdf_data, aes(expression, colour = group)) +
  stat_ecdf(geom = "step", linewidth = .75, pad = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#337C8E", "#AD4E32", "#D5A13B", "#7D5596"),
                       labels = legend_labels) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(100*x, "%"), breaks = c(0,.25,.5,.75,1)) +
  labs(title = "Comparing the full expression distributions",
       x = "Gene expression (provided scale)",
       y = "Participants at or below this expression", colour = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8), plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey94", colour = NA)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
ggsave("figures/additional_ECDF.pdf", ecdf_plot, width = 8.5, height = 8)
ggsave("figures/additional_ECDF.png", ecdf_plot, width = 8.5, height = 8, dpi = 300)

# Record exact versions and actual package citations from this runtime.
packages_used <- c("ggplot2", "dplyr", "tidyr", "patchwork", "rlang", "knitr", "rmarkdown")
write.csv(data.frame(software = c("R", packages_used), version = c(as.character(getRversion()),
  vapply(packages_used, function(x) as.character(packageVersion(x)), character(1)))),
  "results/software_versions.csv", row.names = FALSE)
writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()), "results/sessionInfo.txt")
bib <- "references.bib"
# Make the bibliography self-contained; no external .bib input is required.
writeLines(c(
  "@article{Mirzakhani2016,",
  "  author = {Mirzakhani, H. and others},",
  "  title = {Early pregnancy vitamin D status and risk of preeclampsia},",
  "  journal = {Journal of Clinical Investigation},",
  "  year = {2016}, volume = {126}, number = {12}, pages = {4702--4715},",
  "  doi = {10.1172/JCI89031}",
  "}"
), bib)
refs <- list(Rbase = citation())
for (pkg in packages_used) refs[[paste0("pkg", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "", pkg))]] <- citation(pkg)
for (key in names(refs)) {
  entries <- refs[[key]]
  for (j in seq_along(entries)) {
    b <- toBibtex(entries[j])
    b[1] <- sub("\\{[^,]*,", paste0("{", key, if(j > 1) paste0(j) else "", ","), b[1])
    cat(paste(b, collapse="\n"), "\n\n", file = bib, append = TRUE)
  }
}
```

# Final figures

The following figures retain the supplied expression scale. The fitted line is
unadjusted; its shaded band is a model-based 95% confidence interval for the
fitted mean, not a prediction interval.

```{r final-histogram, fig.cap="Distribution of CYP24A1 expression using 24 bins."}
panels[["CYP24A1"]][["histogram"]]
```

```{r final-scatterplot, fig.cap="Baseline vitamin D and CYP24A1 expression, with an unadjusted linear fit and 95% confidence band."}
panels[["CYP24A1"]][["scatterplot"]]
```

```{r final-boxplot, fig.width=8.2, fig.cap="CYP24A1 expression by pregnancy outcome and vitamin D group. Boxes show median and IQR; whiskers reach observed values within 1.5 IQR of the hinges. All observations and subgroup counts are displayed; jitter is horizontal only."}
panels[["CYP24A1"]][["boxplot"]]
```

```{r final-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=6.4, fig.cap="Ten-gene heatmap with pregnancy outcome and vitamin D annotations. Expression is standardized within each gene. Both genes and participants are ordered by hierarchical clustering using Euclidean distance and complete linkage; the participant dendrogram is displayed. Colors compare relative expression within genes, not absolute expression between genes."}
heatmap_plot
```

```{r final-ecdf, fig.width=8.5, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Empirical cumulative expression distributions for three genes by outcome and vitamin D group. At each x value, the curve gives the fraction of subgroup participants with expression at or below x. The higher-vitamin-D preeclampsia group has only six participants."}
ecdf_plot
```

# Interpretation and limitations

These figures describe exploratory, unadjusted associations and do not establish
causal effects. Distributions may overlap even when their centers differ; visual
comparisons do not replace formal inference. The subgroup with six participants
has limited precision. Heatmap clusters reflect similarity under the chosen
scaling, genes and distance method; they are not validated disease subtypes.
Vitamin D grouping is derived from the continuous vitamin D variable and is not
an independent exposure. The ECDF is an additional-figure candidate: confirm
its eligibility with the teaching team before final submission.
